extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('expr') is passed directly to eval() with only __builtins__ removed. An attacker can craft a malicious expression to execute arbitrary Python code, achieving remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Injection')

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('fragment') is directly rendered by Jinja2 Template.render(), allowing Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). An attacker can use Jinja2 exploitation techniques (e.g., {{ config.items() }}) to achieve arbitrary code execution via template sandbox escape.

User input from request.GET.get('host') is concatenated directly into an os.system() call (ping command). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g., '; rm -rf /' or 'host; ls -la') to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

User input from request.GET.get('name') is used directly as the filename in a file write operation. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../../etc/cron.d/pwn') in the 'name' parameter to write arbitrary files outside the intended BASE_EXPORT_DIR directory, potentially achieving arbitrary file write.

User input from request.body JSON 'filter' field is passed directly to PyMongo MongoClient.find_one() as a query. An attacker can inject malicious JSON query operators (e.g., $gt, $ne) to perform NoSQL injection, potentially extracting data or bypassing access controls.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Database Query (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: User-provided XML from request.body is parsed by lxml with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True enabled. An attacker can inject an XML External Entity (XXE) payload in the XML body to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('lane') or request.POST.get('lane') is passed directly to django.shortcuts.redirect() without validation. An attacker can supply an arbitrary URL (e.g., https://evil.com) to perform an open redirect, potentially for phishing attacks targeting clinic users.

cwe: CWE-601: User Control of Open Redirect

extra.message: Application makes an outgoing HTTPS request to a hardcoded endpoint with ssl._create_unverified_context(), which disables SSL certificate verification. Additionally, the request is made unconditionally without any user input validation, but the disabled verification could allow an attacker who can influence DNS or network to perform SSRF to internal services.

The value of the 'Origin' request header (request.headers.get('origin', '*')) is reflected into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin CORS header with credentials allowed (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true). An attacker can craft a malicious website that sets a trusted origin, causing the browser to return authenticated responses (including session cookies) to the attacker's domain.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Data

extra.message: The response from patient_panel_rebind_041 serializes a workset dict that includes 'is_admin: False' which is then overwritten by user-controlled fields from request.body. This JSON response merges attacker input into a JSON payload, which could allow unauthorized privilege escalation if the JSON response is consumed by a downstream system that trusts its contents.

A hardcoded plaintext password ('DemoPass123!') is used as the password for all demo users created by the seed command. If the application is deployed with this seed, all demo accounts will share the same easily guessable password, enabling unauthorized access if discovered.

A hardcoded default secret key ('dev-only-change-me') is used when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is not set in the environment. This predictable secret key weakens CSRF protection and session security, and may allow session forging or CSRF bypass.

API keys (k.key) are displayed in plaintext in the integrations page template. The value of k.key is rendered directly into the HTML, exposing secret API credentials to anyone with access to the page.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Verifier string comparison (verifier != known[handle]) uses standard Python equality which is susceptible to timing side-channel attacks. An attacker can determine the correct verifier value byte-by-byte by measuring response time differences.

The authorization bearer token from request.headers.get('authorization') is logged unconditionally via logger.warning(). This exposes sensitive authentication credentials in server logs, which could be accessed by unauthorized parties with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' (disabling browser XSS filter) and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string (disabling CSP). These security headers are deliberately stripped, removing browser-side protections against XSS and other attacks.

DEBUG mode is enabled by default (DEBUG = os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', '1') == '1'), which means when DJANGO_DEBUG is not set, Django runs in debug mode. The debug toolbar displays sensitive information including full SQL queries, user data, and stack traces to anyone who can access the admin site.
